---
title: "Signed and absolute gender-gap targets"
subtitle: "5.6 · after the postrank theory book, chapters 4 and 20; KRW’s gender data"
description: "Target-specific posterior probabilities and fixed-order reports for signed and absolute contact gaps."
---

A firm with a large female-name contact advantage can rank low on the signed scale and high on the absolute
scale. Each line connects the same firm's grades under the two targets.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>

<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>

<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["signed-or-absolute"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

The two reports use different posterior pair probabilities. For each target, the app orders firms by expected
rank and searches cuts of that order. To compute probabilities for absolute gaps, the transformation applies
to the gaps throughout the posterior distribution. Signed means or signed direction probabilities alone cannot
recover the absolute report.

- **Both target-specific cards.** Both searches allow at most 4 grades at withholding cost τ .20. Each result
  is labeled “optimal within this order.” A different order can admit different grade reports.
- **Every changed pair.** The “Complete list of changed unordered pairs” keeps every relation that changes from the signed report to the absolute
  report. A direction can appear, disappear or reverse. Each row names both firms and shows the wrong-direction
  probability under the posterior for that target. The signed and absolute risk values answer different questions.
- **All firm summaries.** “All firms in released ID order” keeps all 97 firms together. The table keeps the supplied means and
  central 90% intervals for both targets, their expected ranks, and their chosen grades.

The dots and intervals describe individual firms. The grades depend on the pair probabilities, order, grade cap,
and withholding cost. The report leaves the direction unstated for two firms in the same grade. The absolute-gap
probabilities come from the public postrank data, which supplies separate signed and folded distributions.

Both precision plots use the original sampling SE of the signed estimate. In the plot of absolute gaps, that SE
describes the precision of the original signed estimate. Firms in the middle grade can still differ in their
contact gaps.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The app checks its signed grade assignments against KRW's published gender card.
